prose.def: To serve or worship God (or false gods) through devoted religious service and homage.
prose.article: This verb describes religious service rendered to God—or, occasionally, to idols. In the Byzantine New Testament it is translated "serve" 12 times (63%) and "worship" 5 times (26%), and the two ideas blend together, since the serving in view is always sacred. It carries this religious sense throughout the New Testament; in everyday papyri the word root traces back to a hired servant, but in the Septuagint, where it appears 96 times, it almost always renders Hebrew עָבַד ("serve," 83 times) and consistently means the worship of God or of pagan deities.
